stories.headline: Brandon Aiyuk meets with 49ers, says he's healthy, 'looking to get reinstated'
stories.summary: Brandon Aiyuk met with the Niners on Friday to begin hammering out a path toward a divorce that has been more than two years in the making.
stories.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Though there are still obstacles to work through, the San Francisco 49ers and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk finally appear headed toward a resolution to their tumultuous relationship.

Aiyuk, flanked by his agent Drew Rosenhaus, arrived at the Niners' business offices Friday afternoon to meet with the team and begin hammering out a path toward a divorce that has been more than two years in the making.

In his first public comments to Bay Area media since his knee injury in October 2024, Aiyuk offered a brief statement before he and Rosenhaus headed into the meeting, which lasted about an hour and 15 minutes.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk said. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated to the National Football League."

Aiyuk, who tore the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 20, 2024, hasn't played in an NFL game since. After the Niners voided the roughly $27 million in remaining guarantees in his contract in July 2025 because he didn't show up for rehab check-ins on the knee, he stopped showing up at the team facility and landed on the reserve/left-team list in December.

From there, Aiyuk did not report for any of the offseason program or training camp. Because he is on the left-team list, the only way for Aiyuk to return to play was to apply for reinstatement with the NFL and report to the 49ers.

Aiyuk recently hired Rosenhaus to represent him, and the pair filed for reinstatement in late October. But that hasn't happened yet, in part because the 49ers have been seeking repayment of about $13 million in bonus money that was previously paid to Aiyuk, a source told ESPN. The league informed Aiyuk this week that he needs to repay that bonus money before reinstatement.

Rosenhaus indicated before Friday afternoon's meeting that the hope was to resolve the necessary issues in order for Aiyuk to play again.

"Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team," Rosenhaus said. "Fortunately, he's feeling good physically. He's healthy. He's ready to get back to work. We don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the Niners, but obviously we are here with the right intentions."

If the 49ers and Aiyuk work out a satisfactory agreement that allows for reinstatement, the team would then have three options. They could release Aiyuk, which remains the most likely scenario. They could trade him, which remains the 49ers' preference, though they have been unable to find a trade partner for him throughout the offseason and the deadline is on Tuesday.

Or they could add him to the 53-man roster, something that has seemed like a long shot since general manager John Lynch said in January that Aiyuk played his last snaps for the team.

Coach Kyle Shanahan did not participate in Friday's meeting and made it clear in his news conference earlier in the day that he does not have any interest in a reunion with Aiyuk or in the meeting.

Asked what he would like to see happen in the meeting, Shanahan said he couldn't "care less."

"It's been over for our football team for a long time," Shanahan said. "So, I don't hear much except questions about him today.

"I think it's complicated. I haven't asked one question. I look at this as zero to do with our football team. Anything that has zero to do with our football team, especially during the season, I will give zero thoughts to."

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis to 'step away,' prioritize health
stories.summary: Kristaps Porzingis has announced that he will "step away" from the NBA to prioritize his health. He has not played for the Warriors this season.
stories.body:
Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis has announced that he is stepping away from basketball due to his physical inability to play at the level to which he is accustomed.

Despite the announcement, which is not an official retirement, the Warriors will still be able to use Porzingis' $20 million salary in a trade leading up to February's deadline, per team and league sources.

"I want to show the utmost respect for the Golden State Warriors and work with them to find a solution that makes sense," Porzingis wrote in a social media post Friday.

Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million contract extension with the Warriors in late June and said in the statement that he intended to play this season but that his body didn't respond as he tried to ramp it up for training camp.

Two days before the team's first practice, Porzingis called general manager Mike Dunleavy and told him he wouldn't be reporting. The Warriors let Porzingis remain away from the facility for two weeks, but brought him in for a meeting in early October and anticipated that he'd be around the team.

Porzingis opted to leave the team again after the meeting and has since decided he is stepping away from the NBA entirely. The Warriors have not been delivering him payments on his $20 million salary, and neither Porzingis nor the players' association is contesting that decision.

But the Warriors have no plan to void Porzingis' contract, per team sources, as they continue to survey the league's yet-to-materialize trade market in an effort to eventually improve a team that has jumped out to a 6-3 start with an ongoing six-game win streak.

Porzingis is amenable to a trade and could actually become a relatively appealing contract for a rival team intent on shedding a longer-term salary or saving immediate money. Porzingis has only $3 million guaranteed on his deal next season, and the expectation is that he'd be open to a post-trade buyout that would save a team more than that.

Porzingis has been dealing with persistent health issues after contracting a viral illness while in Boston two seasons ago and has suffered several leg injuries during an otherwise productive 11-year career.

"I'm doing good, but I know what it takes, and I'm not where I want to be to perform at the level I expect of myself," Porzingis wrote.

stories.headline: F1 to make a decision on season finale in Imola next week - sources
stories.summary: Formula 1 has a cut-off date next week to let Italian circuit Imola know whether it is needed to replace two Middle East races as the 2026 season finale.
stories.body:
Formula 1 has a cut-off date next week to let Italian circuit Imola know whether it is needed to replace two Middle East races as the 2026 season finale, sources told ESPN.

As it stands, Formula 1 will finish the year with a triple header of races in Las Vegas (Nov. 21), Qatar (Nov. 29) and Abu Dhabi (Dec. 6).

Those final two races are uncertain, given the U.S-Iran war and ongoing tensions in the region.

Imola is on stand-by to hold a race on Dec. 6 if hostilities in the Middle East escalate in the next few weeks and those last two events need to be cancelled, but the circuit has to know whether the event is taking place in the near future.

Teams ESPN have spoken to are working to an assumption that a decision will be made on Imola next week.

Asked about the situation after Friday practice in Brazil, Haas boss Aayo Komatsu appeared to confirm a deadline.

"I understand Tuesday [Nov. 10] Imola needs be told if we go to Imola or not," Komatsu told Sky Sports on Friday in Brazil.

Imola has already started work on constructing grandstands, with F1 footing the bill.

Sources within F1 have downplayed the idea to ESPN of a fixed date for a decision, as extensions can be given to Imola if F1 feel one is required, but it is clear Imola and the teams need to know before they go to Las Vegas whether that contingency plan still exists.

Sources have told ESPN that the date Komatsu said is broadly accurate and it seems unlikely a decision on Imola will be made much later than the end of next week.

Once the cut-off date is passed, Formula 1 is then in uncharted territory without a back-up option.

- Kimi Antonelli fastest in second practice at São Paulo GP as new world champion

- Ferrari confirms talks to diffuse Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc tension

- George Russell hit with five-place grid penalty for São Paulo Grand Prix

Should there be an escalation in hostilities after Imola has stopped preparing to host a race, it would be likely that F1's season ends with the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Contractually, that hypothetical would nudge F1 into a tricky position, as the commercial deal it has with the sport's 11 teams says the calendar cannot drop below 22 races -- the cancellation of Qatar and Abu Dhabi, with no Imola race back-up, would make the final number 21.

Formula 1 appears to be confident there will not be a big issue in that scenario given the hosting fee paid by the Bahrain Grand Prix to rearrange their race in Malaysia in October.

The sport still intends to race in the Middle East and has been in constant communication with governments in both countries to monitor the situation. The Qatar circuit that is set to be used by F1 next month hosts MotoGP this weekend.

A majority of MotoGP's riders signed a letter ahead of the event expressing their wish not to race, but the championship threatened any riders who boycotted with sporting penalties.

Yamaha has pulled out of the event having found no reason to change its travel policy towards the Middle East. When asked about the MotoGP situation, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said he would be fine with F1 adopting a similar approach.

"Stefano [Domenicali, F1 boss] and Mohammed [Ben Sulayem, FIA president] have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making," Wolff said. "So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that.

"I think that if [MotoGP] riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that.

"Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance."

When Wolff was asked what his policy would be on Mercedes team members expressing a desire to miss the Middle East races, he downplayed how concerned his staff are about going.

"From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised," he added. "It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship. I've always respected that some people didn't want to go to certain Grands Prix, and that's how I see it at the moment."

stories.headline: NHL Power Rankings: Updated poll, plus fantasy hockey surprises for all 32 teams
stories.summary: Another week with the Canes at No. 1, but a big shakeup in the Top 5.
stories.body:
Through another week of the 2026-27 NHL season, the Carolina Hurricanes remain atop the ESPN Power Rankings. But, there are big changes elsewhere in the top five and beyond.

And as a special treat, this week is another fantasy hockey takeover! Sean Allen (East) and Victoria Matiash (West) identified the biggest fantasy hockey surprise -- either good or bad -- for each team.

It's not too late to play ESPN fantasy hockey, with new leagues starting every Monday.

How we rank: A panel of ESPN hockey commentators, analysts, reporters and editors sends a 1-32 poll based on the games through Wednesday. Those ballots are combined to come up with the rankings you see below.

Note: Previous ranking for each team refers to the previous edition, published on Oct. 30. Points percentages are through Thursday's games.

1. Carolina Hurricanes
Previous ranking: 1

Points percentage: 77.78%

Pyotr Kochetkov, G (4.75 fantasy points per game, 18.2% available): Kochetkov has never finished a full NHL season with a save percentage better than .911. He's at .921 this time, with two shutouts and just one regulation loss, and he has grabbed the bulk of Carolina's starts. Behind a team that allows barely 22 shots a game, this one has legs.

Next seven days: vs. CHI (Nov. 7), vs. SEA (Nov. 12)

2. Minnesota Wild
Previous ranking: 3

Points percentage: 73.53%

Ryan Hartman, C (0.92 FPPG, 68.2% available): As the Wild establish themselves as the early team to track down in the Central Division, Hartman is becoming a casual supporting cast member in John Hynes' otherwise formidable lineup. A depressing state of affairs for fantasy managers accustomed to some production from the feisty forward who, suprisingly, isn't satisfying any categories at present.

Next seven days: vs. SJ (Nov. 6), vs. TB (Nov. 7), @ MTL (Nov. 10), @ TOR (Nov. 12)

3. Edmonton Oilers
Previous ranking: 4

Points percentage: 73.53%

Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, C/LW (2.76 FPPG, 29.4% available): Harkening back a few short weeks, there was minimal fantasy interest in the forward, who put up only mediocre numbers the past two seasons and started this campaign on IR. Fast-forward to now and the longest-serving Oiler of all time is picking up points like it's 2022-23. Skating on a power play with McDavid, Draisaitl and Bouchard certainly doesn't hurt.

Next seven days: vs. VAN (Nov. 7), vs. NYR (Nov. 9), vs. PHI (Nov. 11)

4. Boston Bruins
Previous ranking: 2

Points percentage: 73.53%

James Hagens, C (1.98 FPPG, 62.8% available): The 20-year-old has wasted no time making his rookie season a fantasy story. Hagens is on pace to blow past every scoring mark he has ever set, Boston has dominated at 5-on-5 when he's out with Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt, and he has earned power-play time.

Next seven days: vs. FLA (Nov. 8), vs. MTL (Nov. 12)

5. Tampa Bay Lightning
Previous ranking: 6

Points percentage: 73.33%

Charle-Edouard D'Astous, D (2.00 FPPG, 68.8% available): We flagged D'Astous as a pickup two weeks ago, and he has only strengthened his case. His power-play time has nearly tripled from last season, and he's been on the ice for most of Tampa's power-play time lately. Role-driven production on a contender is the kind that sticks.

Next seven days: @ MIN (Nov. 7), @ WPG (Nov. 8), @ BUF (Nov. 11), @ CBJ (Nov. 12)

6. Vegas Golden Knights
Previous ranking: 5

Points percentage: 66.67%

Rasmus Andersson, D (1.52 FPPG, 13.0% available): He isn't anchoring the top power play -- that's a five-forward crew -- and he isn't leading his club in blocked shots -- that's Noah Hanifin -- so all Andersson is accomplishing right now is serving as a functional second-pair defender with five even-strength points in 17 games. A disappointing surprise.

Next seven days: @ BUF (Nov. 8), vs. UTA (Nov. 11)

7. New Jersey Devils
Previous ranking: 7

Points percentage: 68.75%

Arseny Gritsyuk, LW/RW (1.97 FPPG, 56.6% available): Gritsyuk has the best seat in New Jersey, riding with Jesper Bratt and Jack Hughes, and the trio has dominated the scoreboard at 5-on-5. He's also shooting at more than double his career rate, so expect the goals to slow. The linemates are why he should stay rostered when they do.

Next seven days: @ NYI (Nov. 7), @ TOR (Nov. 8), @ WPG (Nov. 10), vs. WSH (Nov. 12)

8. Montreal Canadiens
Previous ranking: 10

Points percentage: 71.88%

Jacob Fowler, G (4.96 FPPG, 21.0% available): The 21-year-old has turned Montreal's crease into his own, going 7-1-1 with a .925 save percentage and two shutouts, including a 46-save gem against St. Louis. He has taken four of the past five starts, and with the Canadiens winning, the work should keep coming.

Next seven days: @ TOR (Nov. 7), vs. MIN (Nov. 10), @ BOS (Nov. 12)

9. Dallas Stars
Previous ranking: 11

Points percentage: 62.50%

Miro Heiskanen, D (1.82 FPPG, 4.4% available): After a more productive start to the season, the Stars' top defenseman has five assists and zero goals (minus-three) to show for eight consecutive contests. Hardly terrible figures, but a disappointing surprise from what was anticipated from a figure expected to keep pace with some of the best fantasy blueliners in the biz.

Next seven days: vs. SJ (Nov. 7), vs. WPG (Nov. 12)

10. Utah Mammoth
Previous ranking: 8

Points percentage: 61.76%

Sebastian Cossa, G (1.33 FPPG, 98.6% available): He's already proving to be more valuable than Karel Vejmelka for his hockey club and fantasy managers alike. After getting his pro pads wet in his first legitimate shot at regular NHL competition, Cossa is establishing himself as a dependable go-to for a strong Utah club with plenty of talent out front. If the Mammoth don't trade for an upgrade in net, the 23-year-old is going to start piling up positive fantasy points quickly.

Next seven days: @ OTT (Nov. 7), @ VGK (Nov. 11), vs. STL (Nov. 12)

11. Colorado Avalanche
Previous ranking: 15

Points percentage: 58.82%

Scott Wedgewood, G (-1.51 FPPG, 29.2% available): With Mackenzie Blackwood back in form, few expected the Avalanche's other netminder to repeat last year's impressive fantasy showing. But this season's flat-out surprisingly poor play from Wedgewood, when offered the occasional opportunity to start for one of the league's better teams, still inspires a shake of the head.

Next seven days: vs. DET (Nov. 7), @ TOR (Nov. 10), @ OTT (Nov. 12)

12. Florida Panthers
Previous ranking: 9

Points percentage: 62.5%

Seth Jones, D (2.55 FPPG, 13.4% available): Jones is scoring like a point-per-game defender, and nothing about it screams fluke. He's logging more than 24 minutes a night with heavy power-play duty, his shot volume is way up and he's converting at his usual rate. Florida's quarterback is back to being a fantasy cornerstone at 32.

Next seven days: @ WSH (Nov. 7), @ BOS (Nov. 8), @ CBJ (Nov. 10), vs. DET (Nov. 12)

13. Ottawa Senators
Previous ranking: 13

Points percentage: 61.77%

Linus Ullmark, G (5.30 FPPG, 9.4% available): Last season's struggles are a distant memory. Ullmark went 7-1-0 with a .945 save percentage before a lower-body injury landed him on injured reserve in late October. He wasn't expected to be out long, so if a frustrated manager in your league cut him loose, pounce.

Next seven days: vs. UTA (Nov. 7), vs. WSH (Nov. 10), vs. COL (Nov. 12)

14. Seattle Kraken
Previous ranking: 12

Points percentage: 63.33%

Mackie Samoskevich, LW (1.84 FPPG, 92.6% available): While many suspected the young skater would enjoy the chance to further spread his wings away from an exceptionally stacked lineup in Florida, fewer projected he would blossom into a such a valuable fantasy performer so quickly. Skating alongside rising star Berkly Catton, the 23-year-old has three goals and four assists on his past six contests.

Next seven days: vs. NYR (Nov. 7), vs. CAR (Nov. 12)

15. Washington Capitals
Previous ranking: 14

Points percentage: 57.14%

Jordan Kyrou, RW (1.98 FPPG, 33.8% available): Kyrou's scoring has outrun his usage. Fifteen minutes a night and fewer than two shots a game don't usually produce this kind of output, he's shooting well above his career mark and Washington has been outscored with him on the ice at 5-on-5. Enjoy the run, but consider trading him away.

Next seven days: vs. FLA (Nov. 7), @ OTT (Nov. 10), @ NJ (Nov. 12)

16. Buffalo Sabres
Previous ranking: 19

Points percentage: 56.67%

Jack Quinn, RW (2.26 FPPG, 32.0% available): Quinn's shooting percentage is running well ahead of his career norm, so some regression is coming. What isn't going anywhere is the role: Buffalo has handed him nearly all of its power-play time lately, and he's skating 19 minutes per game. Even with fewer goals, that's a top-six fantasy winger.

Next seven days: vs. CBJ (Nov. 6), vs. VGK (Nov. 8), vs. TB (Nov. 11), @ CHI (Nov. 12)

17. New York Islanders
Previous ranking: 17

Points percentage: 53.33%

Bo Horvat, C (2.49 FPPG, 7.8% available): At 31, Horvat is on pace to top his career highs, and the usage backs it up: nearly 22 minutes per game, close to four minutes on the power play and three shots a game. His shooting percentage is only a touch above his career norm. Some cooling has already crept in, but this is a legitimate No. 1 center.

Next seven days: vs. NJ (Nov. 7), @ SJ (Nov. 9), @ LA (Nov. 12)

18. Toronto Maple Leafs
Previous ranking: 16

Points percentage: 52.94%

Easton Cowan, LW/RW (1.76 FPPG, 35.3% available): Cowan's second season is shaping up as a breakout. The 21-year-old is on pace to shatter last season's numbers, his shot volume is way up, and Toronto has been dominant at 5-on-5 when he's out with Auston Matthews and Jack Roslovic.

Next seven days: vs. MTL (Nov. 7), vs. NJ (Nov. 8), vs. COL (Nov. 10), vs. MIN (Nov. 12)

19. Nashville Predators
Previous ranking: 20

Points percentage: 59.38%

Ryan O'Reilly, C (2.64 FPPG, 13.8% available): A solid collection of points, sure, but few had the Predators' top centerman boasting seven goals heading into Thursday's tilt with the Avalanche. That trend won't last, O'Reilly's current shooting percentage is unsustainable, but the veteran's all-around fantasy value remains underappreciated.

Next seven days: vs. STL (Nov. 7), @ LA (Nov. 10), @ ANA (Nov. 11)

20. New York Rangers
Previous ranking: 18

Points percentage: 55.88%

Alexis Lafreniere, LW/RW (2.25 FPPG, 12.7% available): Lafreniere is on pace to blow past his career highs. His shot volume is up from last season, and he's getting about three minutes of power-play time a night. The rest is a shooting percentage running well above his career mark. Expect the goals to slow, but the 25-year-old has set a new floor.

Next seven days: @ SEA (Nov. 7), @ EDM (Nov. 9), @ CGY (Nov. 11)

21. Detroit Red Wings
Previous ranking: 21

Points percentage: 50%

Viktor Arvidsson, RW (2.18 FPPG, 41.4% available): Arvidsson's power-play time has nearly doubled from last season, and the 33-year-old has turned it into his best fantasy run in years. His shooting percentage will drift back toward his career mark, but alongside Alex DeBrincat and Emmitt Finnie with steady power-play work, the floor stays high.

Next seven days: @ COL (Nov. 7), @ STL (Nov. 10), @ FLA (Nov. 12)

22. St. Louis Blues
Previous ranking: 23

Points percentage: 50%

Jimmy Snuggerud, RW (1.84 FPPG, 65.5% available): While some of us mused the young winger could flirt with the 40-goal mark in his second year, Snuggerud's early rostership figures suggest we're not a large crowd. Well, even after a less auspicious start, the 23-year-old is on pace for 40-plus, and his fantasy numbers reflect as much.

Next seven days: @ NSH (Nov. 7), vs. DET (Nov. 10), @ UTA (Nov. 12)

23. Anaheim Ducks
Previous ranking: 26

Points percentage: 53.13%

Beckett Sennecke, RW (2.51 FPPG, 14.8% available): The benefits of skating on a line and power play with Cutter Gauthier are coming to fantasy light in real time for the young winger. After accumulating 60 in his rookie season, Sennecke is comfortably on pace to hit the 80-point plateau, including a hefty portion counting with the extra skater.

Next seven days: @ CGY (Nov. 6), vs. PIT (Nov. 8), vs. NSH (Nov. 11)

24. San Jose Sharks
Previous ranking: 22

Points percentage: 44.12%

Macklin Celebrini, C (2.71 FPPG, 0.1% available): Averaging 1.1 real points/game hardly cuts it for a top-five fantasy draft pick overall, especially one who banged out 115 just this past season. Fingers crossed that Wednesday's players' only meeting helps to altogether re-steer the Sharks' offensive ship, led by last year's Ted Lindsay Award finalist.

Next seven days: @ MIN (Nov. 6), @ DAL (Nov. 7), vs. NYI (Nov. 9), vs. PIT (Nov. 11)

25. Columbus Blue Jackets
Previous ranking: 25

Points percentage: 50%

Charlie Coyle, C (1.99 FPPG, 54.9% available): At 34, Coyle is producing at a career-best clip. The difference is opportunity: he's getting more than three minutes of power-play time a night, about a minute more than last season, and he's shooting right around his career rate. That's a late-career bump with a real foundation under it.

Next seven days: @ BUF (Nov. 6), vs. FLA (Nov. 10), vs. TB (Nov. 12)

26. Calgary Flames
Previous ranking: 28

Points percentage: 46.88%

Joel Farabee, LW/RW (2.32 FPPG, 40.2% available): Hands up if you had Farabee on pace for 80 points with the Flames in 2026-27. Right. Yet here we are, watching the former Flyer help Calgary win games by contributing from the top line and power play.

Next seven days: vs. ANA (Nov. 6), vs. PHI (Nov. 8), vs. NYR (Nov. 11)

27. Los Angeles Kings
Previous ranking: 29

Points percentage: 42.86%
