Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

stories.headline: Ferrari confirms talks to diffuse Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc tension
stories.summary: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has said he delivered a clear message to Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on Thursday evening in Brazil as he attempted to clear the air between the two teammates.
stories.body:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur said he delivered a clear message to Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on Thursday evening in Brazil as he attempted to clear the air between the two teammates.

Hamilton demanded "serious talks" with Vasseur and Leclerc last Sunday after his shot at victory at the Mexico City Grand Prix was scuppered by Leclerc's attempt to pass him on the opening lap of the race.

Although no contact was made between the drivers, both ended up off the track, with Hamilton losing a position to eventual race winner Max Verstappen while Leclerc received a penalty for leaving the circuit and gaining an advantage.

The fallout between the two drivers was left hanging after the race as Vasseur traveled back to Ferrari's factory in Maranello and Leclerc returned home to Monaco to be present at the birth of his first child.

Speaking during Thursday's media day, Hamilton said he was still "frustrated" by the incident and vowed not to be "silenced" on the issue.

On Friday, Vasseur confirmed clear-the-air talks had taken place the previous evening, with both drivers reminded of their responsibility to the team.

"We did it," he said. "We did it yesterday evening because I had to fly back to Europe between the two races, but it went well. It was good to discuss, good to clarify my position and their position that it was good to do.

"Now we turn the page and we are focused on the next one."

Asked if new rules had been put in place to avoid a repeat, Vasseur added: "The guidelines are still the same, I think they accumulated perhaps a bit of frustration because they are starting each weekend side by side and you have a kind of accumulation of facts.

"But at the end of the day, the guidelines are always the same. They need to respect each other, that they are two competitors with the fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have respect for the other one. But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track.

"I think we are putting a lot of effort on this and the message was clear and will stay clear."

- George Russell hit with five-place grid penalty for São Paulo Grand Prix

- São Paulo Grand Prix: Lando Norris fastest in first practice in heavily-upgraded McLaren

The incident in Mexico followed a similar first lap battle between the Ferrari drivers at the Italian Grand Prix, which left Hamilton calling on Vasseur to introduce clearer rules between the two drivers.

But the Ferrari team boss, who has long-standing relationships with both drivers, refused to go into details about what was discussed.

"We had a discussion, it has to stay private," he said. "It's a matter of respect also for them and for the team and once again, the most important is the message.

"The message is that we are working for a brand, we are working for sponsors, but I would say probably mainly we are working for the employees of the team and we had a good recovery in terms of performance.

"We came back after Madrid with a much better shape and this is due to the work of the people at home. We all, as a team, we all have to keep this in mind that it's not due to the wind or whatever, it's due to the work of the people and the employees of the company and it was the tone of the message."

stories.headline: Houston Dynamo's Lyle Foster earns Bafana Bafana recall for Kenya AFCON qualifying double-header
stories.summary: Houston Dynamo striker Lyle Foster, on loan from Burnley, earned a recall to the Bafana Bafana squad ahead of November's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying double-header against tournament co-hosts Kenya.
stories.body:
Houston Dynamo striker Lyle Foster, on loan from Burnley, earned a recall to the Bafana Bafana squad ahead of November's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying double-header against tournament co-hosts Kenya.

South Africa will host Kenya at Orlando Amstel Arena on Nov. 13 before travelling for a reverse fixture against Benni McCarthy's Harambee Stars four days later.

McCarthy is Bafana's all-time record scorer with 31 goals. While he was entering the twilight of his career at Orlando Pirates (ironically the club which plays its home games in the venue the teams will square off at on Nov. 13), a young Foster was scouted by Augusto Palacios - the same coach who McCarthy's goals fired to a domestic treble in 2011-12.

Foster has been tipped as a potential heir to McCarthy atop the Bafana all-time scoring charts. However, he has struggled with inconsistent form and mental health issues and was reportedly not at full fitness for Pitso Mosimane's first three games in charge - wins over Guinea, Eritrea and Egypt.

Foster was cut from Mosimane's first preliminary squad, but this time, he has made the 27-man final list alongside his "cousin-uncle" Luther Singh.

Foster's grandmother and Singh's mother are sisters. Singh is the first cousin of Foster's father.

AEL Limassol winger Singh, 29, had been brought back into the Bafana fold by Mosimane for his first three games after falling out of favour under Hugo Broos. Foster, 26, was Broos' usual first choice upfront when available.

Elsewhere, Mosimane has opted to include goalkeeper-captain Ronwen Williams and midfielder Teboho Mokoena despite recent recurring injury struggles with Mamelodi Sundowns. However, their club teammate, Khuliso Mudau, has not recovered in time to be included at right-back.

Thabang Matuludi and the versatile Thapelo Morena - also at Sundowns - are the two right-backs in the squad, with Orlando Pirates' Kamogelo Sebelebele also missing out due to injury.

Mbekezeli Mbokazi unsurprisingly returns at centre-back after an early recovery from his own injury struggles, with Ime Okon (Hannover 96), Olwethu Makhanya (Rangers) and Lebone Seema (Orlando Pirates) the other centre-backs in the squad. This time, there is no room for Nkosinathi Sibisi (Orlando Pirates).

Mbokazi is in familiar company, with the Fire's Puso Dithejane also making the squad as expected after scoring the winner against Egypt and continuing to excel in his role as a winger/attacking midfielder for the Men in Red.

Bafana Bafana squad

Goalkeepers: Ronwen Williams, Sipho Chaine, Ricardo Goss

Defenders: Aubrey Modiba, Samukele Kabini, Fawaaz Basadien, Thapelo Morena, Thabang Matuludi, Olwethu Makhanya, Ime Okon, Lebone Seema, Mbekezeli Mbokazi

Midfielders: Teboho Mokoena, Thalente Mbatha, Sphephelo Sithole, Bathusi Aubaas, Brooklyn Poggenpoel

Forwards: Iqraam Rayners, Lyle Foster, Cassius Mailula, Oswin Appollis, Puso Dithejane, Tashreeq Matthews, Relebohile Mofokeng, Luther Singh, Tshepang Moremi, Siyanda Ndlovu

stories.summary: Blue Jays closer Louis Varland, Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages and Rangers lefty Jacob Latz are among 28 players who are eligible for arbitration as Super 2s.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Blue Jays closer Louis Varland, Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages and Rangers left-hander Jacob Latz are among 28 players with two-to-three years of service time who are eligible for salary arbitration.

Boston right-hander Tyron Guerrero and Colorado outfielder Jordan Beck were the last players to make the so-called Super-2s cutoff, both at 2 years, 133 days. Milwaukee right-hander Quinn Priester had 2 years, 134 days.

The cutoff was up from 2 years, 140 days last offseason.

The top 22% of players by service time with at least two years but less than three are eligible for arbitration as long as they had at least 86 days of service this year. They join the group of three-to-six-year players.

Baseball's collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1 and a management lockout is expected, so it is not clear when proposed salaries will be exchanged or hearings scheduled.

Phillies outfielder Johan Rojas was just under the cutoff at 2 years, 131 days. He started the season at 2 years, 36 days, but he was suspended for 80 games during spring training for a positive test for a banned performance-enhancing substance.

Rojas then had surgery on June 21 to repair a torn UCL in his right elbow, and when his suspension ended four days later, he was placed on the 60-day injured list for the rest of the season.

Other eligible Super 2s are Blue Jays right-hander Spencer Arrighetti, outfielder Nathan Lukes and infielder Davis Schneider, Angels right-hander Sam Bachman, Padres right-hander Jhony Brito, Cubs right-handers Benjamin Brown and Daniel Palencia, Rangers right-hander Jose Butto and outfielder Evan Carter, Guardians right-hander Slade Cecconi, Mariners right-handers Cooper Criswell and Carlos Vargas, Athletics left-hander Hogan Harris, Pirates first baseman Spencer Horwitz, Red Sox second baseman Jahmai Jones, Cardinals right-hander Kyle Leahy and catcher Pedro Pages, White Sox right-hander Jordan Leasure, Tigers outfielder Parker Meadows, Braves left-handers Mitchell Parker and left-hander Danny Young, and Giants right-hander Randy Rodriguez.

Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong had sufficient service time but agreed in March to a $115 million, six-year contract.

St. Louis second baseman Edouard Julien, Milwaukee left-hander Jared Koenig and Detroit outfielder James Outman would have been eligible but were dropped from 40-man rosters this week.

Players were eligible after two years of service from 1974-85, and the threshold increased to three years in 1986. The super 2 class began in 1991 at 17% and it increased to 22% in 2013.

stories.headline: Every AFL club's 2026 draft plans, prospects linked, and live trade options
stories.summary: ESPN's AFL Draft expert Jasper Chellappah looks at every club's plans, its prospects linked, and potential live trade options.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL Draft is two weeks away, and there's a clearer picture on what each club's draft plans are.

You can expect around 65 selections to be made in what has become a deep draft. The mix from 15 to 30 is incredibly even, and the prospects deserving of an opportunity at AFL level runs well past the 65 picks that we'll see across the nights of November 19 and 20.

Amongst the club intel and prospects being targeted at each pick are potential trades to watch for on draft night. Port Adelaide, Carlton and Brisbane will be beholden to where bids land for their star academy prospects, and the selections they hold could be on the move in live draft night trades. Collingwood, Essendon and Adelaide are amongst the clubs mooted to be interested in trading up the order to secure their targets.

It's worth noting that the arrival of Tasmania has repercussions on this year's draft; clubs are more keen to get in now to secure young talent, but it also means draft capital is worth less in future years. Trading up the draft order will be as hard as it's ever been in the live trade era, meaning we could see a host of potential trades never come to fruition.

Included in the details on the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles are the start of second round compensation picks they will receive at the beginning of night two. These come about after a club-tied prospect -- which will be Port Adelaide's Dougie Cochrane -- is taken with a pick prior to their top five selections.

As we approach November's AFL Draft, these are the draft plans, prospects linked, and live trade options for all 18 clubs.

Adelaide
Draft picks: 15, 32, 35, 43, 56, 92, 110

List needs: Midfield quality, outside speed

Adelaide had a quiet trade period and knocked back a swathe of picks for Nick Murray, meaning Hamish Ogilvie's team holds its natural first-rounder plus two seconds to top up a list hunting a premiership. They're valuable selections, but without any manoeuvring they've left themselves behind two Port Adelaide picks in the second round, amongst a nest of talented SA products. Without making a move on draft night the Power will have first dibs on the local crop.

The Crows had a late NGA application for rebounding defender Jake Eime rejected after being alerted to his Indigenous heritage through the SANFL too late in the piece. That shouldn't dissuade them from using a first-rounder on the local product. Eime has the speed and dare to become an offensive weapon off halfback and improve the quality of ball going inside 50.

They'll likely have one of the top three key defenders in the class available, but it won't be Mitch Harris who is firming as a top 10 selection. Clancy Snell would add to their key defensive depth as a high-upside interceptor out of Gippsland, but it would be a touch early for SA captain Kodah Edwards despite his unique mix of forward impact and contested gruntwork.

The best midfielder available at 15 could be Toby Krasna. The Vic Metro on-baller runs both ways and offers some flair with ball in hand on the outside of contests. The versatility and ready-made body of Lochie Burrows would appeal with a view to eventually playing through the midfield. Potential sliders include athletic third tall Wil Malady and tough WA midfielder Leo Steed; the latter should be right in the frame as a piece to immediately push for senior selection.

Late in the second round the lethal left foot of Wil Antrobus should appeal and Gus Kennedy's toughness as a defender with midfield flashes suits. With Adelaide in need of best 23 contenders through the midfield, local products Archie Van Dyk and Memphis Webb will warrant consideration as mature bodies late in the draft. NGA Anthony Long is a backend draft proposition but has serious tricks in the forward half and is deserving of a main list spot.

Brisbane
Draft picks: 21, 27, 28, 45, 79, 97, 115

List needs: Key defender depth

The Lions have another academy gun on their hands, and Caylen Murray has risen to the precipice of the top 10 this season. Granting Keidean Coleman's trade wish effectively ensured Brisbane would have the collateral to match a bid, but they'll have contingencies in place depending on where it lands.

It could come as early as Queensland rivals Gold Coast at pick 8, which would require 1732 points including a 20% loading on grand finalists. Their first two picks only make up 1254 points right now so the Lions will have moves up and down the board with their three second-rounders depending on where the bid lands.

In Murray they're getting a natural Dayne Zorko replacement with excellent ball skills out of defence. His composure under pressure is a highlight and there are midfield traits to be uncovered at the next level.

If the Lions are able to hold onto a second-rounder Jake Soutar presents as the most ready-made defender in the pool. The 20-year-old took out East Perth's fairest and best this season and plays with fantastic aggression in the air, intercepting and kickstarting transition. Darcy Szerszyn is a similar type in the top 30 mix with good athletic traits but underwent an injury-interrupted year.

Benji Van Rooyen is a long-term ruck prospect to look at towards the end of the draft and at 197cm Tate Hodgson has the defensive aptitude to develop into a reliable key defender.

Carlton
Draft picks: 13, 18, 31, 50, 61, 72, 90, 108

List needs: Classy ball users, long-term ruck

Blues fans have been looking forward to this draft for years. Father-son Cody Walker is a bona fide top pick with elite traits through the midfield and he will land at Princes Park no matter where taken, but it's unlikely to be in the first two selections on draft night.

That's a good result for the Blues with live trades in the works depending on where a bid comes. If it lands at pick 3 they'll require 2178 points and their first two selections will equate to 2019 points after an earlier bid on Cochrane. Carlton can do that with a small deficit on their 2027 first-rounder. If Richmond doesn't bid on Walker and he falls to 4 or 5 there will be clubs keen on those selections, and Carlton can capitalise. A slide back to Essendon's 17 from 13 would allow them to match and move their second-rounder up from 31 to 25.

Getting back into the draft early in the second round will give the Blues access to a group of good ball users including Jackson Phillips and Harvie Cooke. Phillips is the running wingman while Cooke is a high-IQ midfielder with talent to play ahead of the ball. George Dimer and Marlon Neocleous are exciting small forwards to consider and Ethan Herbert is the project ruck around this range.

Later in the piece WA's Benji Van Rooyen could appeal as an apprentice to Marc Pittonet and mature-ager Brady Wright would add immediate competition for spots up forward.

Collingwood
Draft picks: 11, 30, 67, 68, 70, 88, 106

List needs: Midfield speed, key position depth

The Pies own a pick in an exciting spot of the draft. There are a cluster of different prospects deserving of top 10 consideration that will be available, but one that may be gone at that point is Sam Gayfer. The nephew of 1990 premiership defender Mick has steadily risen this year as a pack-splitting key forward and the Pies have been one of his biggest fans. Justin Leppitsch would need to part with at least a future first-rounder to a club like Port Adelaide or Gold Coast to ensure they can get him.

If they stay put, Tyson Bradley appeals as the full back of the future and could play senior football early. He's a strong one-on-one defender and reliable distributor with the character to be a future leader of the club. Clancy Snell put in a good performance for Collingwood's VFL side but is an interceptor that may take more time to develop.

Leo Steed is the pick of the midfielders in this bracket, with the WA on-baller offering a mix of defensive application and contested ball-winning that fits alongside Nick Daicos. High-flying forward Wil Malady will be taken around this mark as well.

In the second round the Pies could look to Harvie Cooke and George Gale as midfield options, and mature-age forward options later in the piece include Brady Wright and Jack Slattery who could add immediate depth behind Jesse Hogan and Dan McStay.

Essendon
Draft picks: 1, 17, 25, 80, 98 (plus second round compensation pick)

List needs: Best available talent

The Bombers are at the bottom of their rebuild and hold the first overall selection a decade after taking Andy McGrath at no. 1. Similarly to 2016 and as opposed to recent drafts, there's no consensus top prospect in the open pool.

Expect a bid on Dougie Cochrane at one which Port Adelaide will quickly match, then the draft really begins. Ethan Drever is the slight favourite at no. 2 after a blistering campaign for club and state. The explosive midfielder stayed injury free and produced gaudy numbers enroute to Vic Country's MVP and GWV Rebels's best and fairest. His elite transition game alongside Dyson Sharp and Sullivan Robey will surely appeal.

Arki Butler is a rare archetype to come through the elite pathways and presents as the forward match-winner of the crop. His name has been firmly in contention for the top spot all season and the need to add talent alongside Nate Caddy in the forward 50 is real. Ruck Harry Van Hattum and classy ball user Heath Mellody deserve consideration here as well, but Drever and Butler have the inside lane two weeks out from the draft.

The Dons will have a look at moving up from 17 with additional picks - that could work for either of Port Adelaide or Carlton live on draft night as they look to maximise their draft hands while still matching bids. The key defensive option in the teens is Tyson Bradley, a no-nonsense negator with leadership plaudits. Toby Krasna is in this range as a talented outside midfielder with flair, while George Dimer is in demand as a speedy small forward with tricks.

In the 20s Essendon should be looking at upside swings. Jack Pickett was the leading key forward prospect coming into the year but a season on the sidelines due to an ACL rupture could make him a bargain on night two. Similarly, Koby LeCras adds size and polish out of WA and Lachie Hicks could prove the midfield steal with his blend of speed and endurance as a former track athlete.

The Dons have some interest in Jake Soutar as a mature-age interceptor to replace Jordan Ridley, but will also need to account for a bid on Blake Justice that likely lands towards the back end of the second round. The NGA graduate has a unique mix of speed and size that could even see him attract a bid early on night two.

Fremantle
Draft picks: 19, 40, 60, 63, 78, 96, 114

List needs: Lockdown defender, high-upside talent

Dockers fans don't need reminding how close they've come to that elusive first premiership, but they've continued to build through the draft and keep their premium picks during contention.

At the end of the first round Jake Eime warrants consideration as a halfback dasher alongside Jordan Clark. He takes the game on with speed and can use the ball well while still defending. Jake Soutar has been closely linked as the mature-age option to add to their best 23, but sits between Freo's first two picks on many boards. They would need to trade up or take him with 19.

With 40 being pushed out on the second night they could look towards local talent in Harvey Spawton-Guy whose competitiveness as a key forward stands out. Tom Brown has been overlooked by some but offers reliability in defence and it would be a brilliant result if hard-running midfielder George Gale was still on the board. The goalkicking prowess of Archie Elliott should also appeal in this range of the draft.

The Dockers will be keen to get Finlay Yeo into the club as buzz continues to grow on the NGA talent. He's gifted below his knees and makes things happen through the midfield and up forward. Cam Maynard has offered mercurial moments as a small forward and finished second in the 20m sprint at the combine, but Lucas Robinson has fallen away this season and will be a rookie consideration for Fremantle.

Geelong
Draft picks: 36, 57, 62, 75, 93, 111

List needs: Defensive depth, high-upside projects

The Cats did their work in the trade period by getting Rowan Marshall and Jordan Ridley into the club. Making those moves is made easier knowing Stephen Wells does his best work late in the draft.

Lachie Hicks presents as the high-upside swing in the second round, similarly to Max Holmes in 2020. Hicks has elite athletic pedigree state records through his juniors in track but also put together an impressive campaign as a midfielder. His ball use is preventing him from being a first round option but there's a lot to work with in a good development program.

Billy Wigmore is an excellent interceptor with a build similar to that of Tom Stewart but his draft range begins earlier than pick 36. Sam Dever has been linked as an athletic utility that looks most at home off halfback at 189cm, while the best local product is Noah Williams who played through frustrating injuries all season. He's a smaller inside midfielder with good defensive instincts that could cut his teeth as a lockdown defender.

Gold Coast
Draft picks: 8, 81, 85, 103

List needs: Key position depth

The Suns have Sam Collins turning 33 next year and lost Ben King to free agency. It leaves them exposed at either end over the next few years and they have real need to address their tall stocks with their first open pool top 10 selection since Bailey Humphrey in 2022.

The best key forward in the draft is Sam Gayfer, a brave aerialist possessing the best vertical jump in combine history. His ability to bring the ball to ground with his pack-crashing attitude should appeal to Damien Hardwick. At the other end Mitch Harris and Clancy Snell offer different styles of key defenders. Harris can lockdown on the best key forwards and intercept in his own right, while Snell is the ultra-aggressive interceptor of the pool. Being a country Victorian will help the Suns when assessing their ability to retain talent.

This is the start of Wil Malady's range in the draft, and there's a chance of a slider like Gus Teixeira or Heath Mellody that could make Gold Coast's choice easy.

Local academy product Archie Hill should find his way onto the list as a running defender that plays with energy and dare.

GWS
Draft picks: 9, 20, 26, 59, 77, 86, 104

List needs: Midfield talent, key position depth

It's all about Ethan Matthews on night one, the best Giants Academy prospect to come through the ranks since Tom Green. Matthews is a classy midfielder that racks it up with clean hands and quick decision making off his preferred left foot, and will deservedly be a top 10 pick.

The Giants are in an awkward spot at pick 9, expecting a bid to land before that selection and potentially coming from crosstown rivals the Swans at pick 6. It makes matching the bid easy but look for them to maximise their draft hand by trading on the clock.

In the middle of the second round they will have a few names on the board. George Dimer should be right up there as a high-character small forward with tricks around goal and a willingness to move interstate. Athletic utility Sam Devers could play anywhere across the ground after a strong finish to an injury-plagued year, while the fascinating call will be on Mason McGroder. The Swans Academy defender has foregone a promising international long jump career to pursue football and although raw boasts elite athletic traits in defence. The Giants could make the Swans sweat with a bid in the 20s for the high-upside athlete.

Hawthorn
Draft picks: 29, 37, 71, 94, 107, 112

List needs: Outside run, halfback depth

The Hawks are beautifully set with depth challenging at just about every position. Bringing in Ben King and Zach Merrett made them the biggest winners of the trade period and they still held onto two valuable selections in a deep draft.

A bid on NGA product Keenan Boi is a chance to arrive before their first pick. The half forward plays through contact with strength and makes good decisions under pressure. He's been likened to Sam Powell-Pepper in his attack on the ball and man in the forward half.

In that second round Harrison Chapman offers a unique blend of strong running at 190cm. He looks most at home on a wing where he can use the ball well in space. Albert MacGowan also has the runs on the board to warrant a second round selection as a high-marking wingman. Wil Antrobus is another who can provide transition run, and comes with the added bonus of an elite left foot out of defence that suits the Hawks's style of play.

Hawthorn will be waiting to see if a bid comes for Cooper Hodge. The son of champion Luke looks most at home in defence but has also had promising outings through the midfield in a potential sign of things to come. If a bid doesn't come in the national draft the Hawks will likely take him with their last pick.

Melbourne
Draft picks: 4, 14, 48, 52

List needs: Key defensive talent, ball-winning midfielders

It's been a perpetual cycle of trading into and up draft boards that has reaped rewards for the Dees, who are building their next generation on the fly. They snagged a top 10 pick from the Suns in the Christian Petracca deal last year and made an early move with Port Adelaide to get even higher up the board.

Now, they're in a fantastic position to snap up one of their top four targets. Names in the mix will include Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody. There's every chance those are the first names off the board in the open pool, and you can expect this to be the final place where a bid on Cody Walker would come.

If those three are gone, there will be a fun mix at the top of their board. Similarly to Luke Jackson in 2019, the Dees could opt to give a ruckman the ultimate apprenticeship under the best to do it in the modern era. Harry Van Hattum is deserving of a pick this high - he blends elite athleticism, skill with ball in hand and physicality at a genuine ruck size. The 205cm enforcer plays with aggression in the mould of Brodie Grundy and, similarly to Grundy, may not have the forward craft to play alongside Gawn early on.

Gus Teixeira is the forward-half midfielder with power and scoreboard impact. He can play through centre bounces but will start his career at half forward where he finds a lot of the ball and doesn't need much space to impact.

The wildcard here is Mitch Harris. The premier defender of the pool is equally adept at locking down and intercepting, playing with an air of calm and composure. His range starts here and the SA product is very much in play for the Demons as a ready-made foil for Jake Lever and Dan Turner with senior football under his belt.

At pick 14 Leo Steed should be right in the mix as an in-and-under midfielder that can run hard both ways on the outside. He plays at a high cadence and has a strong body of work in the WAFL. Toby Krasna and Lochie Burrows are other midfield types that deserve consideration, while the other first-round key defenders in Clancy Snell and Tyson Bradley will be options if they opt against Harris earlier.

Brady Wright or Jack Slattery offer immediate forward depth late in the draft and Marcus Prasad is a small forward with clean hands that the Dees could opt for despite not having rights on through their NGA. Benji Van Rooyen could play alongside his brother as he learns the ropes under Gawn.

North Melbourne
Draft picks: 33, 49, 66, 74, 84, 102

List needs: Key position talent, classy ball users

North put their chips in for Nick Blakey and as a result will be without a top-20 pick for the first time since 2019. It signals a new era for the Shinboners as they mount a charge up the ladder under coach Jaymie Graham.

The Roos enter at pick 33, which will extend out a few spots after bids and compensation picks at the top of night two. Billy Wigmore is the type of defender they've been desperate for - the interceptor can play above his size but also roll off smaller forwards to chop out in the air and assist his key defenders. The third tall could play senior football early to add to North's best 23 depth.

Despite a clear need for key position talent, they've taken Matt Whitlock and Blake Thredgold with premium picks and could instead opt for good ball users around the park with an aim to move the ball with more speed. That puts classy halfback Wil Antrobus in the mix as a weapon to utilise out of defence. Further afield lies the upside of rangy outside midfielder Harrison Chapman who has exciting upside as a transition runner, and this is the range busy small forward Marlon Neocleous is expected to be taken. Albert MacGowan and Sam Devers are other running types that could play senior football next year after strong finishes to the year.

Key forward Aidan McCartney has nominated the Roos as a father-son after being in the Swans Academy and has exciting traits despite being sidelined this year with a hip injury.

Port Adelaide
Draft picks: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46, 65, 101

List needs: Midfield depth, key position talent

Night one is all about Dougie Cochrane, the near-consensus top prospect amongst clubs in 2026. Through the Zak Butters free agency compensation and smart manoeuvring in the trade period the Power are well-prepared to match a bid on the academy star at pick one, and have set themselves up with three first-rounders next year with an eye to Zemes Pilot and Louis Salopek.

Selections 7 and 12 remain on the table, but it will take a significant offer for Port to cop a deficit on their 2027 first-rounder. If they moved 7 down in a trade with St Kilda or Collingwood they would then be dealing with a significant deficit on their 2027 selection, so a trade of pick 12 looks more likely. Adelaide and Essendon can trade up from 15 and 17 respectively without impacting Port's ability to match a bid on Cochrane, which could land the Power a future selection or an extra second-rounder this year.

The second round will have a fun mix of local talent. Halfback dasher Jake Eime would be a priority if he was to slide and SA captain Kodah Edwards is right in the frame. His hands in the contest and scoreboard impact up forward offers unique versatility. Ethan Herbert would be a long-term pick with a view to his upside as a ruckman with fantastic contested numbers, and Gabe Patterson presents as a powerful small forward that can break games open. Ball-winners Archie Van Dyk and Memphis Webb are later propositions that could come on quicker than expected in the right environment.

Outside of SA, Jack Watkins has steadily risen this year and would be a smart choice later in the piece as a goalkicking half forward, while Cody Templeton and Marcus Prasad are other smalls in a similar draft range. WA's George Gale is a big-bodied midfielder with excellent endurance in the Willem Drew mould and ball magnet Jordan Knapp has the midfield chops to make it at the next level despite his slender frame. Both will be right in the mix as Port looks to the next generation of on-ballers. Xavier Ladbrook looms as the best key defensive option outside of the first night but will take time to add the size required to play at AFL level.

Richmond
Draft picks: 2, 5, 44, 99 (plus second round compensation pick)

List needs: Best available talent

The Tigers made a big trade to land a second top five pick and maximise their talent before Tasmania enters the competition. It gives them an enviable hand but they'll need to be smart in how they play it with West Coast and Melbourne picking between their selections.

They've been closely linked to Harry Van Hattum. If they have HVH at the top of the board they'll need to use pick 2 on him, with his aggression making him a natural successor to skipper Toby Nankervis. There's every chance they have another name or two ahead of Van Hattum, however, which means intel on Melbourne will be vital here. There's no guarantee he will be available at 5, but that's the limits of his draft range with Richmond to pounce if still on the board.

All of Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody will be considered at pick 2. Drever is the explosive midfielder that fits comfortably alongside Sam Lalor and Taj Hotton as the midfield of the future. Arki Butler is the much-needed firepower up forward to pair with their project talls, and Mellody provides the class and running power off halfback and through the midfield that has been lacking under Adem Yze.

If Drever is taken by Essendon, Butler will be the live favourite to land at Tigerland. He has been at the pointy end of the draft all season as a mercurial forward in the Toby Greene mould.

Van Hattum is the ideal selection if he gets through to pick 5, but Gus Teixeira has plenty of fans and remains in this section of the crop as a damaging forward-half midfielder with power and scoreboard impact.

The Tigers will add a second round pick to their arsenal through a compensation pick on night two and it's a good spot to add run and dare on the outside. Jackson Phillips has a high floor as a wingman with clean hands and good foot skills, George Gale offers a bigger body and the running power to play peripheral positions and Jake Eime should be a real consideration if he slips through as a speedster out of the backline.

NGA prospect Tanner Armstrong may get through to the category B rookie list.

St Kilda
Draft picks: 10, 16, 41, 51, 69, 87, 105

List needs: Key position depth, inside ball-winner

The Saints have undergone a list transformation over the past few years and now own two quality picks after dealing Rowan Marshall to Geelong. They're in a great position to address areas of need and appear unlikely to trade up from these spots.

At pick 10 local product Tyson Bradley will be right in the frame. He has the body to play senior football at some point next year and is reliable in his defensive instincts and composed ball use. He would immediately compete for a spot alongside Cal Wilkie and Jack Silvagni. At the other end of the ground Sam Gayfer and Wil Malady are very different types of key forward prospects. Gayfer is brave and strong in the air with the biggest leap recorded in combine history. Malady can play up the ground with an elite work rate and is dangerous closer to home as an aerialist that butters up at ground level.

Lochie Burrows has been closely linked with the Dragons product providing the toughness, running power and versatility Ross Lyon covets. He can play at either end before eventually moving on-ball, but the Saints would be risking losing out on him if they leave it to pick 16. Leo Steed remains a live option as a pure midfielder that can unlock the runners around him with clean hands in stoppages. The wildcard at this spot is Jack Pickett whose excellent forward craft saw him enter the season at the top key forward prospect before rupturing his ACL.

On night two the Saints can address forward-half woes with talent including powerful SA small Gabe Patterson or exciting goalkicker Marlon Neocleous. Depending on their first two selections, the talls around the mark will include WA's Harvey Spawton-Guy and Knights defender Tate Hodgson.

Sydney
Draft picks: 6, 38, 39, 47, 54, 76, 95, 113

List needs: Key defensive talent, midfield youth

The Swans have their first top 10 pick since taking Logan McDonald and Braeden Campbell in 2020, courtesy of Nick Blakey's exit.

It's a good spot to swoop on any slider out of the top bracket of the open pool. A quality key defensive prospect will be circled on the whiteboard with SA's Mitch Harris the standout this year. He's the all-round package that can lockdown and intercept with safe hands and good closing speed. If there was a name to slide it could be Gus Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder that will eventually become a full-time on-baller.

Expect Sydney to have a good look at a bid on Ethan Matthews out of the Giants Academy, which GWS will promptly match. They may be on the receiving end of an early bid themselves, with Mason McGroder attracting plenty of attention as early as the second round. The champion long jumper has chosen to pursue football and, while raw, he offers incredible upside as a defender that attacks the ball in the air.

As a key forward that can impact right away, Jack Slattery was the best-performed player at the national championships and is just one year older than the draft class. The SA prospect is slightly undersized at 192cm but is a beautiful set shot and creates separation on the lead. His range begins in the 30s. Koby LeCras has a chance to be on the board still after a partial tear of his ACL, but the hard-running forward can play a variety of roles at 192cm including up on a wing or deep forward.

West Coast
Draft picks: 3, 23, 58, 64, 73, 82, 100 (plus second round compensation pick)

List needs: Best available talent

West Coast have another top pick to capitalise on as their list build takes shape. They're right in the frame to snap up the most highly-touted WA prospect since Luke Jackson, with classy midfielder Heath Mellody deserving of a top five pick this year. Beginning his season out of defence, Mellody blossomed on-ball winning the Larke Medal and dominating in patches at WAFL level for Claremont. He has an insatiable work ethic and uses the ball well in space, attributes that pair well alongside Harley Reid and Willem Duursma in the engine room.

It's not a foregone conclusion that the Eagles opt for the local product. Expect them to heavily consider Arki Butler if the goalkicker is on the board still with a real need to add firepower to the forward 50 alongside Jake Waterman. Ethan Drever's power out of the contest will also be coveted and it would be another Vic Country prospect to join the pick one duo.

There's a familial connection with the nephew of 2018 premiership forward Mark LeCras. Koby possesses real talent at 192cm with his running, smarts and goal sense allowing him to play inside 50 or up on a wing. He's a second round option, as is hard nut Noah Williams whose courage in the clinches and capacity to play with defensive intent has value. Local product George Gale has the frame to play early through the midfield and wings in this range as well.

The Eagles will look to trade one of their second round selections for a 2026 first-rounder with an eye towards capital for a Chad Warner play. Add to it that James Artemis is a top prospect in the crop out of Western Australia.

It comes with the list crunch - West Coast has three spots to use at the national draft and will be keen to secure father-son Harper Banfield after missing on brother Charlie last year. Halfback Garrison Kenh and father-son Noah Braun will be rookie considerations.

Western Bulldogs
Draft picks: 42, 53, 55, 83, 89, 91, 109

List needs: Reliable role players, small forward depth

The Dogs did their work at the trade period by securing Zak Butters via free agency and a multi-club trade. It means they enter proceedings late on night two with an eye towards talented NGA forward Khaled El Souki. He's rated around the top 20 but may slide due to the depth of the crop which will make for an easier time matching a bid for the Dogs.

They addressed their key defensive dearth with Jordon Butts but should still have a look at Xavier Ladbrook as a long-term piece, and there are more defensive options in Darcy Szerszyn and Billy Wigmore that could be available later in the draft. Wigmore is a local Western Jets product alongside Lachie Hicks whose athletic traits through the midfield are tempting.

stories.headline: Kiwis make crunch Ponga call for Tonga RLWC semifinal
stories.summary: Kalyn Ponga is set to complete a miraculous recovery from a broken forearm to feature in New Zealand's World Cup semi-final with Tonga.
stories.body:
Kalyn Ponga is set to make a remarkable return for New Zealand's semifinal with Tonga, 23 days after the Newcastle captain suffered a broken arm.

There were fears Ponga's tournament was over after one game when the fullback, making his Test debut in the World Cup opener against Australia on October 15, was substituted off with a forearm fracture.

Ponga hasn't played since but has remained in Kiwis camp.

And after undergoing a strenuous recovery process, the Newcastle fullback will be named on Stacey Jones' teamlist for Saturday's semifinal at McDonald Jones Stadium.

Jones confirmed Knights hooker Phoenix Crossland, who hasn't played since being suspended for his tackle on Nathan Cleary in the NRL preliminary final, will also come into his 19-man squad.

"We'll make that decision when the time comes but he'll be in our 19-man squad," Jones said.

"(Crossland) has had a really good week, he'll be part of our six-man bench and he's been part of our squad for three years now.

"It's a big boost and being then from here, from Newcastle, so it's pretty special to come back here and play for the Kiwis at their home ground.

"The main thing for him (Ponga) was making sure he ticks every box and is confident to play."

Ponga started at fullback against the Kangaroos in the tournament opener and will replace Keano Kini if Jones chooses to deploy the Newcastle No.1 from kick-off.

Jones would not be drawn on whether Ponga, who is expected to wear a protective arm guard against Tonga, would start against Tonga.

"I've never had that type of injury or anything in my career before, but I think a few of the boys Xavier Willison and Jahrome Hughes have," said captain James Fisher-Harris.

The return of Crossland and Ponga means two players originally listed in Jones's 19-man squad will miss out, with the Kiwis coach set to make a decision on Friday evening.

The Kiwis reached the semi-finals four years ago and the narrow loss to Australia in Leeds still burns Fisher-Harris, who is anticipating a strong turnout from Tongan supporters.

"We're looking forward to the battle and the crowd is always amazing," said the Warriors prop.

"We've spoken a little bit about our history and things and it comes down to moments.

"I thought we played really well in that game and a few moments cost us, we've learned from that."
